title: Cross-cutting: error responses (die_error)
description: gitweb die_error is invoked ~102 times producing styled 400/403/404/500 pages with the correct HTTP status. Provide a domain-error -> (status,page) mapping rendered through the render layer and used by EVERY capability (unknown project/object -> 404, forbidden -> 403, malformed params -> 400, internal -> 500). Gherkin-first, one scenario per status. Depends on render; the web boundary depends on this. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.
close_reason: die_error mapping split into two concerns: status_for(&DomainError)->HttpStatus classifier (NotFound=404, Invalid=400, Forbidden=403, Backend=500) and error_page(status,message,detail)->Markup renderer; error_response ties them together. Added DomainError::Forbidden to complete the 403 vocabulary gitweb needs. New render::error module + HttpStatus value type (5 gitweb statuses incl. 503 for request-level gates). Gherkin: features/render/error.feature, one scenario per status + escaping/detail edges, red->green, 63/63 render scenarios green. Modernized error styling (.error in style.css). Workspace tests/clippy -D warnings/fmt all green. Unblocks hlm (web boundary).

title: Project conventions & architecture (READ FIRST)
description:
Port of git's gitweb (Perl CGI) to Rust. Source of truth for behaviour: ~/IdeaProjects/git/gitweb/gitweb.perl (8491 lines, 30 actions in %actions, ~20 %feature toggles) and static/gitweb.css. ALWAYS read the relevant gitweb sub before implementing.

NON-NEGOTIABLE CONVENTIONS:
- Hexagonal/ECB. Workspace crates: domain (entities+ports+use-cases, framework-free), git adapter (gix), render (templates->HTML), web (axum boundary + config), app (composition root). Dependencies point INWARD only.
- BDD/TDD, Gherkin ALL THE WAY DOWN. EVERY capability produces features at THREE layers: features/domain (pure rules), features/usecase (use-case via ports + gix-built fixtures), features/web (axum end-to-end). All run by cucumber as harness=false test targets. Strict red->green: feature, then step defs, watch them FAIL on assertions, THEN production code.
- gix adapter gets CONFORMANCE specs over gix-built fixtures.
- Test discipline: cyclomatic complexity 1 (no loops/branches in tests), cover zero/one/many (two counts as many).
- Git backend: gix only, behind a Repository port. NO unsafe (unsafe_code=forbid). Fixtures built WITH gix (no git binary at test time).
- HTML MODERNIZED: semantic HTML5, framework-free templates, fresh CSS. Match gitweb behaviour/information, not markup.
- SECURITY: validate + access-control (see safety bead) BEFORE any fs/repo access; no path traversal; respect repo export rules.
- ESCAPING: rely on template-engine auto-escaping for HTML; handle esc_url/esc_path explicitly; guard deliberate raw-HTML sinks (README.html, highlight output).
- ENCODING: to_utf8 + fallback encoding + binary detection live in domain primitives.
- ERRORS: every capability maps domain errors to die_error-style 4xx/5xx via the error bead.
- Explicit type annotations on variables and lambda params.

DONE (not a bead): workspace scaffold + cucumber harness + first domain slice (Age::humanized/class) green vs age_string/age_class.

title: gix adapter: commit search (message/author/committer/grep/pickaxe)
description:
Implement the Repository ports search operation in the gix adapter: commits matching a query, paged (skip + limit), across the SearchKind variants: commit message, author identity, committer identity, file-content grep, and pickaxe (commits that add or remove the pattern). Read the relevant gitweb search code first and match its behaviour.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (gitweb_in_rust-sor): zero / one / many matches; a pattern matched under each search kind; a pagination boundary; a query with no matches; case and pattern handling consistent with gitweb.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Pure adapter. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-a10; unblocks search.
close_reason: Implemented the four commit-listing search facets in the gix adapter (crates/git/src/repository.rs): message/author/committer as a HEAD-rooted, case-insensitive substring (gitweb --grep/--author/--committer --regexp-ignore-case --fixed-strings) and pickaxe as a case-sensitive occurrence-count delta over the rename-aware diff (git log -M -S), reusing the existing diff() machinery. Conformance: crates/git/tests/search.rs + features/search/commit_search.feature, 17 scenarios green (many/one/zero per facet, author!=committer, pickaxe count-delta + case-sensitivity, pagination boundaries). Removed the dead SearchKind::Grep variant: gitweb's grep facet returns file/line hits at one revision, not commits, so it cannot share search()->Vec<Commit>; split into gitweb_in_rust-7ua with its own port shape. Full workspace cargo test/clippy -D warnings/fmt green. Commit message ends with 13s.

title: gix adapter: project last-change age (git_get_last_activity)
description:
A project's 'last change' is the age of the most recent commit on any of its branches — gitweb's git_get_last_activity. The projects-list page shows it as a sortable age column and the summary page shows it too, so it is per-project metadata the discovery (gitweb_in_rust-2kf) and repo-overview (gitweb_in_rust-otk) capabilities both consume. Read gitweb's git_get_last_activity (and get_branch_refs for which refs count) before implementing.

WHAT: surface, as part of a project's metadata, the commit timestamp of its most recently updated branch. Carry it on the domain ProjectInfo entity (crates/domain/src/model/project_info.rs), extending the gitweb_in_rust-reh slice that already resolves description/owner/category/cloneurl. The adapter must expose the raw commit TIMESTAMP, not an age relative to 'now': the clock belongs to the view layer, kept out of the adapter so conformance stays deterministic and any golden output never flickers. The existing domain Age entity already turns an elapsed-seconds value into gitweb's age string and CSS bucket, so the view computes (now - timestamp) and reuses it.

PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): a repo with a single branch; several branches where the most recent commit wins; an empty / unborn repo with no commits (no activity -> the field is absent); only the configured branch refs count (gitweb's get_branch_refs, default refs/heads), not tags.

This needs a gitweb-fixtures ProjectRoot extension to build a repo with multiple branches at distinct, pinned timestamps so 'most recent wins' is testable deterministically.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Pure adapter + one ProjectInfo field. Split out of gitweb_in_rust-reh.
close_reason: Implemented git_get_last_activity as a ProjectInfo.last_activity carrier (Option<i64> committer epoch) + gix adapter selection. Domain: with_last_activity/last_activity() on ProjectInfo (raw timestamp; view computes now-epoch via Age). Adapter most_recent_branch_time(): max committer time over refs/heads (.all()+starts_with per gix-adapter-gotchas; into_fully_peeled_id->commit->to_signature.epoch), absent for unborn/empty. Fixtures: RepoBuilder::open_at + ProjectRoot::add_empty_repo/add_branch_at/add_tag_at (pinned distinct timestamps). Conformance in metadata.feature: zero(unborn)/one/many(most-recent-wins)/tags-excluded. 17/17 metadata green, full workspace 196+ scenarios green, clippy -D warnings + fmt clean. Commit ends with bead id.

title: Cross-cutting: input safety + repository access control
description: SECURITY-CRITICAL. gitweb: validate_pathname/validate_refname (~19 sites); check_export_ok/$export_ok/$export_auth_hook/$strict_export (~8 sites). Reject path traversal / directory escape on project, file (f=) and ref/hash (h=,hb=) params BEFORE any filesystem or repo access. Enforce repo visibility: only serve repos allowed by export rules (git-daemon-export-ok file or configured auth hook). Reject malformed refs/object ids. Gherkin-first WITH negative scenarios (../ escapes -> 400, non-exported repo -> 404). Blocks the web boundary. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.
close_reason: Input safety + export visibility as two pure-rule domain modules (model/safety.rs: SafePath/SafeRef per is_valid_pathname/ref_format/refname; model/export.rs: ExportPolicy::permits per check_export_ok + strict_export). Gherkin-first with traversal/malformed negatives + export gate matrix; 90->131 scenarios green, clippy/fmt clean, no unsafe. Commit bc78981. Note: fs-probing adapter to build RepoFacts + wiring of SafePath/SafeRef at the web boundary remain downstream (hlm/a10/reh).

title: gix adapter: blame (line-by-line attribution)
description:
Implement the Repository ports blame operation in the gix adapter: for a path as of a given commit, attribute each line to the commit that last changed it, producing the domain Blame entity. Read the relevant gitweb blame code first and match its behaviour.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (gitweb_in_rust-sor): a file with a single author versus many authors; lines introduced by the root commit; attribution that follows the file across a rename; a missing path or commit (error).

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. blame_data is a format-stable endpoint, so it is additionally covered by golden differential conformance per gitweb_in_rust-sor when that endpoint lands. Pure adapter. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-a10; unblocks blame.
close_reason: Implemented Repository::blame in the gix adapter via repo.blame_file with rename-following (rewrites=Some(default)) to match gitweb's plain 'git blame -p', which follows whole-file renames by default. New conv::to_blame flattens gix's hunk entries into one domain BlameLine per final line (1-based orig/final line numbers, trailing-newline chomped, to_utf8/latin1 decode), sorted into final-file order. Mirrors gitweb's pre-checks: missing commit and missing path -> NotFound. New conformance target crates/git/tests/blame.rs over gix-built fixtures, 7 scenarios green, attributions pinned against real 'git blame -p': single-commit file, three-author layered edits, rename-following, empty file (zero lines), orig/final line numbering, missing path, missing commit.

title: gix adapter: unified diff (patch) text
description:
Produce the textual unified diff (patch) for the diff-bearing views — NOT the structured difftree. gitweb_in_rust-fmz already delivers which paths changed (status/modes/ids); this is the actual @@-hunk body with the +/- lines, file headers, and mode/rename/copy/binary notices.

Two consumers need it: (1) the format-stable plain endpoints that must match real gitweb byte-for-byte — commitdiff_plain, blobdiff_plain, patch, patches (golden differential conformance, gitweb_in_rust-sor); (2) the client-side @pierre/diffs viewer, whose parsePatchFiles consumes a standard unified diff.

Behind the Repository port: given a commit (vs its parent) and given two blobs, yield a unified diff. READ THE GITWEB CODE FIRST — git_patchset_body and the diff-tree -p invocation: how it emits the diff/index/--- /+++ headers, the "Binary files ... differ" notice (not a hunk), rename/copy headers with "similarity index NN%", and mode-change lines.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (gitweb_in_rust-sor): create / delete / modify; file-mode change; binary blob (notice, not hunk); rename and copy with the correct similarity-index header; symlink (120000) and submodule/gitlink (160000); empty diff; non-UTF8 content; and merge / multi-parent combined (--cc) hunks once gitweb_in_rust-l06 lands (the combined case may follow l06).

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. The plain endpoints are format-stable, so the bytes are additionally pinned by golden differential conformance per gitweb_in_rust-sor when those endpoints land. Pure adapter. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-fmz (and gitweb_in_rust-l06 for combined).
close_reason: Unified diff (patch) text delivered in two clean halves. DOMAIN (crates/domain/src/model/patch.rs): a pure formatter owning git's patch FORMAT as a rule — diff --git header, extended headers (old/new mode, new/deleted file mode, similarity index, rename/copy from/to), index line (emitted only when blob identity changes; trailing mode only when both sides share one), --- /+++ (suppressed for content-less changes), binary notice, @@ ranges with git's ,1-omission and 0,0-creation rules, and \ No newline at end of file. 16 domain scenarios. ADAPTER (crates/git: conv.rs to_file_patch/text_hunks over gix-diff's UnifiedDiff+slider heuristics; repository.rs patch()+side_content()): feeds the formatter from real repos behind the new Repository::patch port method; binary via domain is_binary, gitlinks synthesized as 'Subproject commit <id>', symlinks diffed as text with the no-newline marker, non-UTF8 lossy. 11 conformance scenarios over gix-built fixtures. Full suite green (153 domain + 11 patch + all others), clippy -D warnings + fmt clean. SCOPED OUT (as the bead anticipated): combined --cc merge hunks follow l06; byte-exact index abbreviation and inexact/copy similarity index are endpoint/my1 concerns; the path-filtered blobdiff variant is a thin filter over patch() to land with the blobdiff endpoint. Commit ends with the bead id.

title: Capability: snapshot
description: gitweb action: snapshot. Archive a tree-ish as tgz/tbz2/txz/zip per the snapshot feature config; correct content-type + filename. Drives Repository archive port. Gherkin-first. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: gix adapter: content grep search (git grep at one revision)
description:
Implement gitweb's 'grep' search facet (searchtype=grep, git_search_files): content search at ONE revision via 'git grep -n -z', listing each matching FILE with its line NUMBER and the matching line TEXT. Read git_search_files in gitweb.perl before implementing.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD: split out of gitweb_in_rust-13s. The Repository port's search() returns Vec<Commit> and serves the four commit-listing facets (commit/author/committer/pickaxe). grep is fundamentally a different operation: it does not list commits, it lists file/line hits within a single tree, so it cannot share that return type. 13s removed the dead SearchKind::Grep variant; this bead adds grep's own port shape.

WHAT: a new Repository port operation that, given a revision (tree-ish, gitweb's $hash/$co{'tree'}) and a pattern, yields the content matches. Each match carries the file path, the 1-based line number, and the matched line's text. gitweb caps output at 1000 matches and then shows a 'listing trimmed' notice; binary files are reported as a match with no line text ('Binary file (.+) matches'). The match-highlighting (wrapping the matched substring in <span class=match>) is a VIEW concern and belongs in render, not the adapter — the adapter returns the raw line text and lets the boundary decide highlighting. A new domain entity (e.g. GrepMatch { path, line_no, text } with a binary-file variant) carries the result; it is plain data, so per the ports-vs-entities rule it gets conformance over fixtures, not its own domain feature, unless a pure rule (line splitting / binary detection) emerges.

PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): zero / one / many matches; matches spread across several files (grouped per file, file order stable); multiple matches in one file (each line listed); a binary file match (reported, no text); a non-UTF8 / fallback-encoded line; case handling consistent with gitweb's git grep default; the 1000-match trim boundary. gix has no built-in 'git grep'; implement by walking the tree's blobs at the revision and scanning lines, mirroring git grep's default (literal, case-sensitive unless gitweb's regexp toggle — which, like the commit searches, is not in the port).

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Pure adapter + one domain match entity + one port method.
close_reason:
Content grep (git_search_files / git grep -n -z -F at one revision) via BDD, red->green at two layers.

DOMAIN (pure rule): crates/domain/src/model/grep.rs — GrepMatch{Line{path,line_no,text}|Binary{path}} + GrepResults{matches,trimmed} + GREP_MATCH_LIMIT=1000 + file_matches(path,content,pattern). Per-file rule: empty pattern matches nothing; binary file (NUL via is_binary) reported once iff its bytes contain the literal pattern, no text; text file yields one Line per matching line, 1-based via split_inclusive (git's line model incl. final unterminated line), literal CASE-SENSITIVE substring (git -F, no -i) so a line lists once however many occurrences, matched line decoded via to_utf8/latin1 fallback. 13 domain scenarios in features/domain/grep.feature.

PORT: Repository::grep(revision: tree-ish, pattern) -> GrepResults added to crates/domain/src/port/repository.rs.

ADAPTER: crates/git/src/repository.rs grep() — walks tree_leaves (path order, recursive), greps only Regular/Executable blobs (symlinks & gitlinks skipped, matching real git grep on a tree), delegates per-file to file_matches, applies gitweb's cap (len>LIMIT -> truncate+trimmed, early return). 10 conformance scenarios in crates/git/features/grep/content_grep.feature over a gix-built mixed-mode fixture (text/binary/non-UTF8/symlink/gitlink/executable/subtree) + cap-boundary fixture; new tests/grep.rs harness, [[test]] in Cargo.toml.

Parity vs gitweb_in_rust-sor edges covered: zero/one/many, grouped-per-file-in-tree-order, multi-match-per-file, binary (no text), non-UTF8 fallback, tree-ish accepts commit OR tree id, 1000-match trim boundary. Highlighting + untabify left to render (view concern). All harnesses green, clippy clean, fmt clean.

title: Capability: blame
description: gitweb actions: blame, blame_incremental, blame_data. Line-by-line attribution; incremental (progressive) + data endpoints feeding client JS. Drives Repository blame port. Gherkin-first. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: CI: enforce tests, clippy, fmt, no-unsafe
description: Verification is not optional. CI running cargo test (every cucumber harness across crates), cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, and a guard that unsafe stays forbidden. Gate merges on green. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: gix adapter: repository open + object reads
description:
Pure-Rust gix adapter (crates/git, crate gitweb-git): opens a repository and implements the object-reading half of the Repository port: HEAD, reference enumeration by prefix, revision resolution, object kind, and commit / tree / blob / tag reads, mapping gix failures to domain NotFound / Invalid / Backend. Includes the adapter crate scaffold and the gix-to-domain conversion module that the remaining adapter operations reuse.

Conformance via Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, covering zero / one / many plus the parity edges (merge commit, every file mode, binary blob, empty tree, unborn HEAD, missing object or ref, wrong-kind reads).

The remaining adapter operations are split into sibling beads: history (eog), tree-to-tree diff (fmz), blame (5o3), snapshot archive (i95), search (13s), and ProjectStore discovery (cnm). See those for scope.
notes: Sliced adapter. DONE (slice 1): crates/git (gitweb-git) scaffolded; GixRepository::open + object reads — head (incl. unborn->NotFound), references(prefix) via all()+string-prefix filter, resolve (rev_parse_single), object_kind, find_commit (author/committer via domain Signature::parse on a rebuilt ident line; merge detection), find_tree (every file mode incl. symlink/gitlink/exec via FileMode::from_octal), find_blob (kind-checked, binary heuristic), find_tag (annotated, tagger optional). Error mapping: missing->NotFound, wrong-kind->Invalid, else Backend. Conformance: crates/git/features/conformance/object_reads.feature (25 scenarios, zero/one/many + sor edge cases) over gix-built fixtures, red->green. REMAINING slices (all still return labelled Backend errors, no conformance yet): history+pagination+path-filter, tree-to-tree diff (incl. combined/--cc merge diffs + rename/copy), blame, archive/snapshot bytes, search (grep/pickaxe/ident/message). ALSO TODO: ProjectStore impl (list + open) — separate file crates/git/src/project_store.rs.
close_reason: Object reads + crate scaffold + conv module done and verified (cargo test/clippy/fmt green), commit 9ead36d. Remaining adapter operations split into sibling beads eog/fmz/5o3/i95/13s/cnm.

title: Domain primitives via TDD
description: Pure domain value objects mirroring gitweb helpers, Gherkin-first. Age (DONE). Remaining: file mode -> filetype + permission string (file_type/file_type_long/mode_str), ObjectId + abbreviation, git ident/Signature (name/email/time/tz), string helpers (chop_str, chop_and_escape_str), ref-name shortening (strip refs/heads|tags|remotes/), email obfuscation (email-privacy), AND text-encoding handling (to_utf8 + $fallback_encoding + binary-content detection, used by file/diff rendering). Each: feature -> red -> impl -> green; zero/one/many. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.
close_reason: Domain primitives via BDD red→green, 7 new pure value-object modules under crates/domain/src/model + Gherkin features (51 new scenarios, 220 steps total green): file_mode (mode_str/file_type/file_type_long incl. gitlink-before-S_IFMT ordering + octal guard), object_id (sha1/sha256 validation + 7-char abbreviation), signature (parse_commit_text ident split: rightmost-epoch greedy + name/optional-email), chop (chop_str right/left/center, char-based, word-aware add_len slack + ellipsis fillers), ref_name (strip refs/heads|tags|remotes, annotate other namespaces), email_privacy (hide_mailaddrs <local@domain> -> <redacted>), encoding (to_utf8 + latin1 fallback) and binary (NUL-byte detection, deliberate documented divergence from Perl -T). chop_and_escape_str intentionally deferred to the render adapter (it is chop_str + esc_html + CGI span — HTML concerns, not domain). cargo test/clippy -D warnings/fmt all green.

title: gix adapter: ProjectStore discovery (list + open)
description:
Implement the ProjectStore port in the gix adapter: list the projects discoverable under the project root, and open one project by name for reading (returning a Repository). This is the bare discovery and open mechanism only. Read the relevant gitweb project-enumeration code first and match its behaviour.

Scope boundary: per-project metadata (description, owner, category, README.html, cloneurl, fork detection) and multi-source config precedence are NOT in this bead; they live in gitweb_in_rust-reh, which builds on top of this discovery.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (gitweb_in_rust-sor): zero / one / many projects; nested repositories under the root; a non-repository directory ignored; opening a name that does not exist (error); a path-traversal attempt in the name rejected, respecting the input-safety rules from the closed safety bead.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures (several fixture repos under a temp root), red->green. Pure adapter. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-a10; unblocks project discovery (alongside reh).
close_reason: Implemented GixProjectStore (ProjectStore port): list() walks the project root recursively, recognises a git repo by check_head_link (HEAD present or symlink into refs/heads/), prunes descent on a found repo (gitweb File::Find behaviour), returns Projects by store-relative '/'-joined name, sorted for determinism. open() validates the name via domain SafePath (rejects ..-traversal/absolute/NUL -> Invalid), confirms the dir is a repo (-> NotFound if absent), opens a GixRepository. Added gitweb-fixtures ProjectRoot (multi-repo layout under one temp root) + RepoBuilder::init_at (caller-owned dir, _dir now Option). Red->green conformance: crates/git/features/discovery/project_discovery.feature (11 scenarios: zero/one/many, nested, non-repo ignored, no-descend, open success incl. nested, NotFound, traversal+absolute rejected) all green; full workspace test/clippy -D warnings/fmt clean.

title: gix adapter: commit history (rev-list, pagination, path filter)
description:
Implement the Repository ports history operation in the gix adapter (crates/git): the commits reachable from a starting revision, optionally filtered to those that touch a given path, returned as one page (skip + limit, per the Page contract). Read the relevant gitweb rev-list code first (the invocations behind shortlog / log / summary and the feeds, with max-count / skip and an optional pathspec) and match its behaviour.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (see gitweb_in_rust-sor): zero / one / many commits; the first page and the last partial page at a pagination boundary; a path filter that selects a subset versus a path that matches nothing; a root commit (no parents) at the end of history; multi-parent (merge / octopus) ancestry ordering.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures (gitweb-fixtures), strict red->green, in the existing adapter conformance style. Pure adapter, no web or render coupling. Builds on the adapter base in gitweb_in_rust-a10; unblocks repo overview and history & feeds.
close_reason: Implemented Repository::history in the gix adapter via rev-list newest-first by commit time (Sorting::ByCommitTime(NewestFirst)), Page skip/limit windowing, and first-parent path-touch filtering matching gitweb's parse_commits. Extracted gix->domain commit mapping into conv::read_commit (shared with find_commit). New BDD conformance target 'history' (13 scenarios): order, one/many, root-at-end, pagination first/last-partial/past-end, path subset/add/matches-nothing, octopus ancestry ordering. All harnesses + clippy -D warnings + fmt green; no unsafe.

title: Request model: gitweb actions + param/PATH_INFO parsing into a validated Request (domain rule)
description:
Split out of gitweb_in_rust-hlm: the PURE-DOMAIN request rule that the axum boundary uses, modelled in the domain crate per the constitution's 'three layers, domain first' rule (gitweb_in_rust-0et) — exactly as gitweb_in_rust-hlm's own note asks for config-precedence to be a pure domain rule with its own Gherkin.

Read gitweb.perl's %actions table, @cgi_param_mapping, evaluate_path_info, evaluate_and_validate_params, is_valid_action/is_valid_pathname/is_valid_ref_format/is_valid_refname before implementing.

WHAT this delivers (pure, framework-free, with domain-layer Gherkin):
- An Action entity covering gitweb's full %actions route table (blame, blame_incremental, blame_data, blobdiff, blobdiff_plain, blob, blob_plain, commitdiff, commitdiff_plain, commit, forks, heads, history, log, patch, patches, remotes, rss, atom, search, search_help, shortlog, summary, tag, tags, tree, snapshot, object, opml, project_list, project_index). Parse from the wire name (is_valid_action), render back, and a needs-project predicate (opml/project_list/project_index are the 'those below don't need project' set).
- A Request value object holding gitweb's long-named fields (project, action, hash, hash_parent, hash_base, hash_parent_base, file_name, file_parent, page, order, searchtext, searchtype, snapshot_format, extra_options, ...), built from the short->long @cgi_param_mapping.
- Validation -> DomainError mapping mirroring evaluate_and_validate_params: invalid action -> 400; file_name/file_parent via SafePath; hash/hash_parent/hash_base/hash_parent_base via SafeRef (reuse model/safety.rs); page digits-only -> 400; searchtype [a-z] only -> 400; searchtext < 2 chars -> 403; extra_options against the allow-list per action.
- The PURE part of PATH_INFO decomposition: the ref(:path)(..parentref(:parentpath)) regex and the action-defaulting rules (empty/trailing-slash -> tree; file form -> blob_plain/blobdiff_plain; parent ref -> shortlog; @wants_base tree/history -> hash_base vs hash), plus the snapshot-format-from-suffix stripping. Project resolution FROM PATH_INFO walks the filesystem (check_head_link) and is NOT here — it belongs to the web/usecase layer behind the ProjectStore port.

PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): zero/one/many params; missing action defaulting; the ref:path colon form and the A..B parent-range form; snapshot suffix extraction; every validation failure mapped to the right status. Strict red->green, cyclomatic-1 tests, zero/one/many.

Leaves gitweb_in_rust-hlm to own only the axum wiring: HTTP<->Request adapter (incl. the filesystem project-walk for PATH_INFO), Response adapter, static asset + MIME serving, and the GLOBAL config chain.
close_reason: Pure-domain request rule complete across three capabilities, all red->green: (1) model/action.rs — Action entity for gitweb's full %actions route table, parse/as_str/needs_project (commit eca936b); (2) model/request.rs — Request value object + the query-param half of evaluate_and_validate_params, short->long mapping with each field validated to the DomainError whose status mirrors gitweb's die_error (commit 4414811); (3) model/path_info.rs — the pure half of evaluate_path_info: action-peel, first-'..' parent split, first-':' ref/path split, action defaulting (tree/blob_plain/blobdiff_plain/shortlog/@wants_base) and snapshot-suffix stripping (this commit). 269/269 domain scenarios green, clippy -D warnings + fmt clean workspace-wide. Deliberately scoped OUT and left to hlm: the filesystem project-prefix walk (check_head_link) and the query/PATH_INFO merge+precedence. Deferred: three view-pref params (ds/by_tag/js — no consumer yet, would be dead fields) and searchtext regexp-syntax validation (lands with search, where the pattern is compiled).

title: gix adapter: two-tree diff + rename detection
description:
Implement the Repository ports diff operation in the gix adapter: the difference between two trees, where an absent from-side means diff against the empty tree (for example a root commit), producing the domain Diff entity. This is the heaviest adapter operation: gitweb leans on it across roughly 118 merge / combined-diff sites and 120 rename / copy sites. Read the relevant gitweb diff code first (the diff-tree usage behind commitdiff / commit / blobdiff) and match its behaviour.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (gitweb_in_rust-sor): added / deleted / modified files; file-mode changes; symlinks; submodule (gitlink) changes; binary blobs (reported as differing, not as text hunks); rename and copy detection with similarity; a root commit (against the empty tree); and the combined / multi-parent diff for a merge commit (the change relative to all parents at once).

This bead may warrant further splitting into basic two-tree diff, rename / copy detection, and combined-merge diff; that decision is left to the implementer.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. The format-stable commitdiff_plain output is additionally verified by golden differential conformance per gitweb_in_rust-sor when that endpoint lands. Pure adapter. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-a10; unblocks commits & diffs.
close_reason: Two-tree diff + rename detection in the gix adapter, red->green. Domain: ChangeStatus::from_modification (git's M-vs-T rule, FileMode::same_type) + added/deleted/renamed constructors, with domain Gherkin (crates/domain/features/domain/change_status.feature). Adapter: conv::to_diff_entry maps gix Change->DiffEntry (filters tree entries to match diff-tree -r; null-oid/000000 for absent sides), GixRepository::diff peels both sides to trees (None=empty tree for root commits), runs diff_tree_to_tree with Rewrites::default() (renames @50%, gitweb's -M), sorts by path. Conformance: crates/git/features/diff/tree_diff.feature (14 scenarios: add/delete/modify, mode-change M, file->symlink T, symlink/gitlink add, binary, root-vs-empty, rename sim=100, subdir leaf-only, missing object->NotFound). All harnesses+clippy+fmt green, unsafe still forbidden. SPLIT (decision left to implementer per bead): combined --cc merge diff -> gitweb_in_rust-l06 (needs domain Diff extension; blocks 2os); copy detection -> gitweb_in_rust-my1 (gix 0.84 copy tracking doesn't fire; inexact similarity).

title: Repository + ProjectStore ports and entities

ProjectStore: list projects under projectroot, open(name)->Repository. Entities: Commit, Tree/TreeEntry, Blob, Tag, Reference, Diff, Project. Domain error type. These ports are the seam that lets use-cases be tested with fakes. See conventions bead.

DomainError vocabulary (NotFound/Invalid/Backend), HTTP mapping left to the error bead. Pure-rule entities got red->green domain Gherkin: Commit.is_merge/title/title_short (parse_commit_text), ChangeStatus::parse (parse_difftree_raw_line status token), ObjectKind::parse. title: gix fixture builder for tests
description: Test-support module that builds deterministic git repos WITH gix (no git binary): init repo, write blobs/trees/commits with pinned author/committer name+email+date so OIDs are stable across runs, create branches/tags. Consumed as the Given in usecase + web Gherkin specs. This bead also de-risks the gix 0.84 object/commit WRITE API (highest-uncertainty surface). See conventions bead.
close_reason: Built gitweb-fixtures crate: RepoBuilder writes deterministic git objects+refs with gix 0.84 (init_bare, blob, tree, commit, branch, lightweight+annotated tag, set_head, id_of, read_blob). De-risked the gix write API: empirically confirmed write_blob/write_object/reference/edit_reference, and that gix ASSERTS canonical tree-entry order (panics otherwise) so the builder sorts via gix's git-semantics Ord. 14 conformance scenarios green (97 steps), anchored on git's canonical empty-blob e69de29 / empty-tree 4b825dc ids, covering special modes (exec/symlink/gitlink/dir), canonical ordering, merge/multi-parent commits, non-UTF8 byte round-trip, unborn HEAD, branches and tags. Strict red->green (stubbed to null oids, watched 11 assertion failures, then implemented). clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, unsafe forbidden.

title: Web boundary: axum router + request/response + config
description: axum standalone server. Route table for all 30 actions; parse gitweb params (p=project, a=action, h/hb=hash(base), f=file) AND pathinfo-style URLs; Response adapter; static asset + MIME serving; config loading (projectroot, site name, feature toggles; GITWEB_CONFIG-equivalent). Composition root wiring gix adapter + use-cases + render. See conventions bead.
notes:
Request-model carve-out: the PURE request rule is DONE in gitweb_in_rust-evs (closed) — model/action.rs (Action = %actions route table), model/request.rs (query-param validation -> DomainError, the evaluate_and_validate_params half), model/path_info.rs (the pure evaluate_path_info decomposition). What is OWNED HERE for the request side: the axum HTTP<->Request adapter that (a) walks the filesystem to resolve which PATH_INFO prefix is the project (check_head_link), (b) calls PathInfo::parse on the remainder ONLY when the query string did not pin an action, and (c) merges query params + PATH_INFO with gitweb's precedence into the validated Request. Plus: Response adapter, static asset + MIME serving, and three still-deferred view-pref params (ds/by_tag/js) if a consumer needs them.

Multi-source config split: the PER-PROJECT gitweb.* layer is done in gitweb_in_rust-reh (read straight from each repo's git config). What is OWNED HERE is the GLOBAL config chain — loading built-in defaults < GITWEB_CONFIG_COMMON < GITWEB_CONFIG / GITWEB_CONFIG_SYSTEM, with per-project overriding all — because loading those global files is inbound configuration at the composition root, not the git adapter's job. Model the precedence (first-defined-wins over an ordered list of sources) as a pure domain rule with its own Gherkin, then wire the actual file loading here.

title: gix adapter: snapshot archive bytes (tgz/tbz2/txz/zip)
description:
Implement the Repository ports archive operation in the gix adapter: the bytes of a snapshot archive of a tree in each enabled format (tgz, tbz2, txz, zip, per the ArchiveFormat variants). Read the relevant gitweb snapshot code first and match its behaviour.

Parity edges the Gherkin must cover (gitweb_in_rust-sor): each format; an empty tree; a tree containing executables, symlinks, and submodules represented correctly in the archive; deterministic, reproducible bytes so the same tree always yields the same archive.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Snapshot output is format-stable, so byte-exact bytes are additionally covered by golden differential conformance per gitweb_in_rust-sor when that endpoint lands. Pure adapter. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-a10; unblocks snapshot.
close_reason: Implemented Repository::archive in the gix adapter, BDD red->green over gix-built fixtures: 18 scenarios across all four formats (tgz/tbz2/txz/zip) green. New module crates/git/src/archive.rs drives gix worktree_stream -> worktree_archive (Tar/TarGz/Zip native, pure-Rust flate2/zlib-rs + rawzip) and compresses the raw Tar for tbz2/txz with pure-Rust backends (bzip2 libbz2-rs-sys, lzma-rust2 with unsafe 'optimization' OFF) -- no C FFI, no unsafe in our crates, consistent with the zlib-rs precedent. modification_time pinned to a constant so every format is byte-reproducible (the bead's core parity edge). Entry representation matches git archive's default: regular 0644 / exec 0755 / symlink-as-symlink / subtree recursed / gitlink(submodule) skipped; empty tree -> well-formed file-less archive; non-tree-ish rejected as Invalid via require_tree (gitweb 400). Parity DEFERRED to the snapshot endpoint per the bead: download filename + --prefix (snapshot_name) and byte-exact-vs-git-archive golden bytes -- gix streams BFS (tree's files before subtrees') vs git's DFS, deterministic but a different order. gix gotcha: worktree-archive is not a default feature AND gix does not forward gix-archive's container features, so a direct gix-archive dep with tar/tar_gz/zip is required (recorded in memory). cargo test (whole workspace) + clippy -D warnings + fmt all green.

title: gix adapter: combined multi-parent merge diff (--cc)
description:
Combined diff of a merge commit against ALL its parents at once, the way gitweb renders a merge with 'git diff-tree -c/--cc' (parse_difftree_raw_line's '::'-prefixed branch: nparents, a per-parent vector of from-modes/from-ids, and a per-parent status string). Split out of gitweb_in_rust-fmz, which delivered the two-tree diff + rename detection.

BLOCKED ON A DOMAIN-MODEL EXTENSION: the current domain Diff/DiffEntry (crates/domain/src/model/diff.rs) models only an ordinary two-tree diff (single from-side). Its module doc says so explicitly: 'Combined diffs against multiple parents are a later capability and are not modelled here.' This bead must FIRST extend the domain entity to carry a combined entry (n parents, per-parent from-mode + from-id + status, single to-mode/to-id/path), with its own domain Gherkin, THEN implement it in the gix adapter over gix-built fixtures.

Parity edges (gitweb_in_rust-sor): a 2-parent merge; an octopus (3+ parent) merge; a path changed vs some parents but not others; combined add/delete; interaction with the commitdiff/commit views. Read the gitweb '--cc for multiple parents' code (around the diff-tree '--cc'/'-c' invocation and the combined branch of parse_difftree_raw_line) before implementing.

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Pure adapter + domain extension. Builds on gitweb_in_rust-a10 and gitweb_in_rust-fmz; needed by full commitdiff parity (gitweb_in_rust-2os).
close_reason: Combined multi-parent merge diff (git diff-tree -c/--cc). Domain: extended crates/domain/src/model/diff.rs with CombinedDiff/CombinedDiffEntry/CombinedParent (per-parent from-mode+id+status, single to-side) plus pure rules is_deleted/has_history/not_deleted/nparents mirroring gitweb's combined-diff loop; added ObjectId::is_null/null_like; domain feature combined_diff.feature (4 scenarios). Port: added Repository::combined_diff(commit). Adapter: gix has NO native combined diff, so composed it from per-parent path-keyed tree_leaves() comparisons (tree.traverse().breadthfirst.files()) applying git's rule 'show a path only if it differs from EVERY parent'; conformance merge_diff.feature (6 scenarios: differs-from-both, matches-one-parent-omitted, combined add, combined delete, octopus 3-parent, missing-commit). Path-keyed: rename/copy detection across combined merges deferred (matches gitweb raw output). All harnesses green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Commit ends with bead id.

title: Capability: search
description: gitweb actions: search, grep, pickaxe, search_help. Commit/author/committer search, file-content grep, pickaxe (changes introducing/removing a string), search help page. Drives Repository grep/pickaxe + history filters. Respects search/grep/pickaxe feature toggles. Gherkin-first. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: gix adapter: copy detection (-C / gitweb @diff_opts)
description:
Rename+copy detection for the two-tree diff, matching gitweb configured with copy detection. gitweb's default is @diff_opts = ('-M') (renames only); '-C' (copies, implies -M) and '-C --find-copies-harder' are opt-in via configuration. Split out of gitweb_in_rust-fmz, which delivered renames-only at git's default 50% similarity.

WHY DEFERRED: investigation during fmz showed gix 0.84's tree-diff copy tracking does NOT surface copies for the obvious fixtures — with rewrites.copies = Some(Copies { source: FromSetOfModifiedFiles | FromSetOfModifiedFilesAndAllSources, .. }), an exact copy was still reported as a plain Addition, not Change::Rewrite { copy: true }. This bead must first establish (via a probe/fixtures) the exact conditions under which gix emits a copy, or conclude that copy detection must be computed on top of gix's changes, before wiring it behind the Repository port.

ALSO: similarity for INEXACT copies/renames. fmz reports 100 for an exact rewrite (gix sets diff: None when source_id == id) and falls back to gix's DiffLineStats.similarity otherwise; that ratio is NOT git's similarity index. If copy/rename similarity must be byte-exact (e.g. the 'similarity index NN%' line in patch output), that exactness belongs here or in the patch endpoint, not in the raw difftree adapter.

Parity edges (gitweb_in_rust-sor): exact copy; near-copy above/below threshold; copy of an unchanged source vs a modified source; copy + rename in one diff. Map Change::Rewrite { copy: true } -> ChangeStatus::Copied (a domain ChangeStatus::copied(similarity) constructor is needed; ChangeStatus already has the Copied kind and parses 'C<score>').

Conformance: Gherkin over gix-built fixtures, red->green. Pure adapter (+ small domain constructor). Builds on gitweb_in_rust-fmz.
close_reason: Copy detection wired behind the Repository port. Probe established gix 0.84's exact copy behaviour (recorded in gix-adapter-gotchas memory): gix DOES emit Rewrite{copy:true}, source selection matches git (-C = modified set, --find-copies-harder = all sources), but with 3 divergences — it shadows a modified copy-source's own M, computes similarity against the post-image, and skips a lone-copy commit (has_work gate). Added domain port value RenameDetection {RenamesOnly(-M)/Copies(-C)/CopiesHarder(--find-copies-harder)} threaded through diff()/patch(). Adapter uses a TWO-PASS MERGE: renames-only base (faithful M/A/D/R, no shadowing) + a copies pass that only yields copy pairs, then reclassifies the matching addition to Copied with the from-side = source PRE-image (from tree), exact pre-image == to-side -> 100, else gix's similarity hint. Conformance: 9 new copy scenarios in features/diff (renames-only ignores copies; -C finds modified-source copy + ignores unchanged source + keeps source's own M; harder finds exact unchanged-source copy + near-copy above threshold, rejects below; rename+copy together), red->green. ChangeStatus::copied() already existed; no other domain change. Lone-copy has_work gate documented as a known gix limitation. All harnesses green, clippy+fmt clean.

title: gix adapter: filesystem owner fallback for project owner
description:
gitweb resolves a project's owner in priority order (git_get_project_owner): the projects-list-file owner, then the gitweb.owner config value, then — as a last resort — the operating-system owner of the repository directory (get_file_owner: the passwd display name of the directory's uid). The first two sources are done in gitweb_in_rust-reh; this is only the final filesystem-owner fallback. Read gitweb's get_file_owner and git_get_project_owner first.

WHAT: when neither the projects-list file nor git config names an owner, fall back to the display name of the user that owns the repository directory on disk, so the projects list and summary still show an owner the way gitweb does.

PARITY EDGES (gitweb_in_rust-sor): an owner set by file or config (the fallback is NOT consulted); no file/config owner (the fallback IS used and yields the directory's user); a uid with no passwd entry (the owner is gracefully absent, not an error).

CONSTRAINTS: honour the workspace's no-unsafe rule and its aversion to needless dependencies when resolving uid -> name. The result is non-deterministic across machines, so the conformance must not assert a real username — make the uid->name resolution injectable/seamable so a spec can pin it, and test the PRECEDENCE and the missing-entry behaviour rather than a literal name.

Conformance: Gherkin, red->green. Pure adapter. Low-priority parity nicety split out of gitweb_in_rust-reh.

title: Cross-cutting: HTTP conditional GET / caching
description: Conditional GET / caching at the web boundary. gitweb emits Last-Modified and honours If-Modified-Since for feeds, snapshots, and blobs (~5 sites). Required behaviour: when the client's cached copy is still current, respond 304 Not Modified instead of resending the body; otherwise serve normally with appropriate freshness metadata. Gherkin-first incl. the 304 path. Depends on the web boundary. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: Capability: repo overview
description: gitweb actions: summary, heads, tags, remotes, tag. Summary (recent log + refs + description/README), heads/tags/remotes lists, single annotated-tag view. Drives Repository ref+commit reads. Gherkin-first. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.
notes:
Per-project metadata this page consumes is already delivered: description /
owner / category / cloneurl by gitweb_in_rust-reh (ProjectStore::info ->
ProjectInfo), last-change age by gitweb_in_rust-3y0. What remains OWNED HERE for
the summary page: reading and showing $GIT_DIR/README.html. That is a deliberate
raw-HTML sink (gitweb injects the file's bytes verbatim) — guard it per the
conventions bead (gitweb_in_rust-0et); it is NOT list metadata, which is why it
was deliberately left out of reh.

title: Feature: syntax highlighting
description:
gitweb "highlight" feature: syntax-highlighting of FILE/BLOB bodies (the file-browsing view, gitweb_in_rust-t06).

The DIFF-body half is already delivered by gitweb_in_rust-rhf (@pierre/diffs is Shiki-based), so this bead narrows to blob/file highlighting — and must FIRST evaluate reusing pierres CodeView/Shiki (~280 languages, already vendored for rhf) with a per-file language hint, rather than standing up a separate server-side highlighter. title: Project metadata & multi-source config
description: Subsystem behind ProjectStore. gitweb: git_get_projects_list / $projects_list file-vs-scan (~21 sites); git_get_project_config + description/owner/category + README.html + cloneurl + fork detection (~9 sites). Read project list from a projects_list file OR by scanning projectroot; per-project metadata from filesystem (.git/description, cloneurl, README.html) + git config (gitweb.description/owner/category/url); category grouping; fork relationships. Config precedence: built-in < GITWEB_CONFIG_COMMON < GITWEB_CONFIG / SYSTEM < per-project. Gherkin-first. Depends on ports; project-discovery and repo-overview depend on this. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.
notes:
PROGRESS (session 2026-06-07), still in_progress.

DONE (BDD red->green, commits 216ec5e, 5617cc6, cd4f6cb):
- Project list both ways: scan (was already done) AND from a $projects_list file
  (GixProjectStore::from_list_file; file-mode list() filters to safe + real repos,
  check_export_ok's check_head_link; preserves file order).
- Per-project metadata via git_get_file_or_project_config: description, category,
  cloneurl from the repo file else gitweb.<key> config; multi-valued gitweb.url.
- Owner precedence (git_get_project_owner): projects-list-file owner > gitweb.owner.
- Domain pure rules with features: url::unescape (CGI::Util::unescape),
  forks::partition_forks (filter_forks_from_projects_list, component-wise trie),
  project_info::{descr_short(chop), category_or, group_by_category},
  projects_list::parse_project_line.

  set_description/remove_description/set_category/set_clone_urls/set_gitweb_config/

REMAINING in reh:
- git_get_last_activity: most-recent branch-commit timestamp (for-each-ref
  --sort=-committerdate over refs/heads). NEEDED BY BOTH dependents (2kf age column,
  otk summary). Adapter should return the epoch (deterministic); age-from-now is a
  view concern. Carry as ProjectInfo.last_activity: Option<i64>. Needs a ProjectRoot
  fixture extension for multi-branch / custom-timestamp repos to test "most recent wins".
- OS-file-owner fallback (gitweb get_file_owner, uid->name): lowest-priority owner

DELEGATED OUT of reh (correct hexagonal boundary, do NOT do here):
- README.html raw-HTML content -> repo overview (otk); it is a deliberate raw-HTML
  sink belonging to the summary page, not list metadata.
- Global config chain built-in < GITWEB_CONFIG_COMMON < GITWEB_CONFIG/SYSTEM <
  per-project: the FILE LOADING of the global gitweb config is inbound config at the

close_reason: Delivered the metadata+config subsystem behind ProjectStore: scan + projects_list-file listing, per-project description/owner/category/cloneurl via git_get_file_or_project_config, owner precedence, fork detection, category grouping, projects-list line parsing — all BDD red->green (commits 216ec5e, 5617cc6, cd4f6cb). Remaining work split into dedicated beads: last-change age -> gitweb_in_rust-3y0, filesystem owner fallback -> gitweb_in_rust-o09. Delegated by architectural boundary: README.html -> otk (raw-HTML summary sink), global GITWEB_CONFIG chain -> hlm (inbound config at composition root).

title: Diff & blob viewing via the vendored @pierre/diffs client viewer
description:
Render diffs (and syntax-highlight code) in the browser with the @pierre/diffs client component instead of a server-side colouriser/highlighter — reusing the integration already proven in ~/IdeaProjects/cc/pipe-cli/apps/diff-viewer (same hexagonal + maud stack).

WHY (reject the alternative): @pierre/diffs (Shiki-based, ~280 languages) parses a standard unified diff client-side and renders a themed, syntax-highlighted, light/dark diff view as a web component. Reusing it beats reimplementing gitwebs format_diff_line colouriser, and it also covers the diff-body half of gitweb_in_rust-qz0 (syntax highlighting). Zero NIH.

WHAT this delivers:
- The diff-bearing web views serve a standard unified diff (from gitweb_in_rust-5ps) at an endpoint, plus a host page (rendered by gitweb_in_rust-rpg) that boots the viewer; the viewer fetches the diff, runs parsePatchFiles, and renders it. An empty diff shows a clean "no changes" state.
- The @pierre/diffs bundle is vendored REPRODUCIBLY from a pinned upstream commit (built + re-bundled to self-contained browser ESM), git-ignored not committed (~11 MB of Shiki grammars), behind a documented one-time refresh script. Mirror apps/diff-viewer/scripts/vendor-pierre.sh and static/vendor/README.md. The binary must still serve and stay inspectable when the bundle is absent (warn, do not fail).
- Light/dark theming follows the viewers OS setting.

Parity: every diff edge case must render correctly through the viewer — merge / combined (--cc) incl. octopus, rename / copy, file-mode change, binary, empty, non-UTF8 (gitweb_in_rust-sor).

Test discipline: behaviour specced at the web layer where observable (endpoint content-type/shape, host markup, empty-state, error->status mapping); purely-client rendering covered by DOCUMENTED MANUAL CHECKS, consistent with gitweb_in_rust-h2t.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION to copy/adapt: ~/IdeaProjects/cc/pipe-cli/apps/diff-viewer — src/routes/api.rs (raw unified diff as text/plain), src/views.rs (maud host page), static/boot.js (parsePatchFiles + CodeView), static/app.css (chrome only; pierre styles the diff), scripts/vendor-pierre.sh (pinned @pierre/diffs 1.2.1, bun build + re-bundle).

Reshapes diff presentation in gitweb_in_rust-2os and subsumes the diff-body half of gitweb_in_rust-qz0; sits alongside gitweb_in_rust-h2t (client JS / vendoring).

title: Render layer: framework-free templates + new CSS
description:
Modernized semantic HTML5 rendering of domain view-models ONLY (no git or web-framework coupling). ENGINE: maud (compile-time, auto-escaping by default; PreEscaped is the raw-HTML safe-sink by construction) — decided, see the diff-viewer reference + the render-stack memory; confirmed to build on this toolchain (edition2024 / rust1.93, same as pipe-cli).

Scope:
- The esc_* escaping family (esc_html / esc_html_nbsp / esc_path / esc_url / esc_param / esc_attr / esc_path_info, with control-char visualisation) — DONE: 28 BDD scenarios vs gitweb behaviour in crates/render/src/escape.rs.
- Site chrome (header/nav/footer), fresh CSS replacing gitweb.css, favicon/logo.
- A raw-HTML safe-sink so intentionally-raw HTML (e.g. README.html) renders without double-escaping and cannot inject from untrusted input (likely maud Markup/PreEscaped).
- Relative-age values styled by recency (domain AgeClass -> CSS class).

title: Parity acceptance: edge-case matrix + differential conformance
description:
Defines what 'feature parity with gitweb' actually means; referenced by every capability.

EDGE-CASE MATRIX. A capability's Gherkin is not parity until it covers these domain edges, not just the happy path (gitweb leans on them heavily: ~118 merge/combined-diff sites, ~120 rename/copy sites): merge / multi-parent (combined / --cc) diffs incl. octopus; rename + copy detection with similarity; file-mode changes; symlinks (mode 120000); submodules / gitlinks (mode 160000); binary blobs (inline vs download); empty / unborn repo (no HEAD); non-UTF8 content with fallback encoding; pagination boundaries; missing/invalid object or ref.

PARITY ORACLE. HTML pages are MODERNIZED, so they are verified behaviourally only. gitweb's format-stable endpoints, however, must match real gitweb output and are verified by GOLDEN differential conformance: capture reference output from the original gitweb.perl ONCE into committed golden files (no perl needed at test time), diff ours against it. In scope: commitdiff_plain, blob_plain, patch, patches, project_index, rss, atom, opml, blame_data. Build the golden harness + corpus; wire each endpoint as it lands. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: Capability: file browsing
description: gitweb actions: tree, blob, blob_plain. Directory listing with modes/sizes, blob view with line numbers, raw blob with correct MIME and binary-vs-text handling (inline vs download). MUST render the tree-entry edge cases: symlinks (mode 120000) and submodules / gitlinks (mode 160000) shown distinctly; empty tree. Drives Repository tree/blob reads + encoding primitive. Gherkin-first; parity per gitweb_in_rust-sor. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.

title: Feature: ctags / content tags
description: gitweb 'ctags' feature: per-project content tags + tag cloud on the project list. See gitweb_in_rust-0et.
